papers.title: Code uniqueness of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in spatial chromatic model
papers.abstract: The spatial chromatic model (SCM) is a novel entity-oriented spatial data model proposed in recent years. Spatial tessellations formed by SCM have been applied in preliminary analyses of spatial point pattern recognition,spatial topology, and Voronoi diagram generation. Unlike previous spatial tessellation models, a key feature of SCM is that each subspace (cell) possesses a chromatic code, which serves as the foundation for various theoretical analyses and applications of SCM. The uniqueness of cell cluster codes in SCM constitutes an important property of the model. Previous studies have demonstrated the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 2-cell and 3-cell connected disjoint clusters. Building on this analysis of connected cluster code characteristics, this paper proves the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters. The proof results and the new concepts introduced in this study help further refine the spatial chromatic model and provide a theoretical foundation for its subsequent applications.

papers.title: Realizing graph automorphisms as geometric symmetries of straight line drawings
papers.abstract: Given a finite graph $G$, we characterize the automorphisms and automorphism groups of $G$ that can be realized as geometric symmetries and symmetry groups of straight line drawings of $G$ in the plane. In doing so, we correct a previous version of this characterization from the literature. As an application, we show that the graphs recently constructed by the first two authors to disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which have orders $16{,}464^k$ for each positive integer $k$, are the first known vertex-transitive graphs with no non-trivial realizable geometric symmetries. We also construct infinite families of graphs that exhibit all possible kinds of geometric symmetry.

papers.title: On the Vertices of Delta-modular Polyhedra
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a polytope defined by the system $A x \leq b$, where $A \in R^{m \times n}$, $b \in R^m$, and $\text{rank}(A) = n$. We give a short geometric proof of the following tight upper bound on the number of vertices of $P$: $$ n! \cdot \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\text{average}}} \cdot \text{vol}(B_2) \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi n}} \cdot \left(\frac{2 \pi}{e}\right)^{n/2} \cdot n^{n/2} \cdot \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\text{average}}}, $$ where $\Delta$ is the maximum absolute value of $n \times n$ subdeterminants of $A$, and $\Delta_{\text{average}}$ is the average absolute value of subdeterminants of $A$ corresponding to a triangulation of $P$'s normal fan. Assuming that $A$ is integer, such polyhedra are called $\Delta$-modular polyhedra. Note that in the integer case, the bound can be simplified via the inequality $\Delta_{\text{average}} \geq \Delta_{\min} \geq 1$, where $\Delta_{\min}$ is the minimum absolute value of subdeterminants of $A$ corresponding to feasible bases of $A x \leq b$. For this, we prove and use a symmetric variant of Macbeath's theorem. Additionally, we give a direct argument based on prior results in the field, showing that the graph diameter of $P$ is bounded by $O\bigl(n^3 \cdot \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\min}} \cdot \ln (n \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\min}}) \bigr)$. Thus, both characteristic of $P$ are linear in $\Delta/\Delta_{\min}$. From an algorithmic perspective, we demonstrate that: Given $A \in Q^{m \times n}$, $b \in Q^m$, and an initial feasible solution to $A x \leq b$, the convex hull of $P$ can be constructed in $O(n)^{n/2} \cdot m^2 \cdot \frac{\Delta}{\Delta_{\text{average}}}$ operations. For simple polyhedra, the dependence on $m$ reduces to linear; Given $A \in Z^{m \times n}$ and $b \in Q^m$, the number $|P \cap Z^n|$ can be computed in $O(n)^n \cdot \frac{\Delta^4}{\Delta_{\text{average}}}$ arithmetic operations.

papers.title: An Unconditional Lower Bound for the Active-Set Method in Almost-Linear Programming
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every fixed $\epsilon\in(0,1]$, the active-set method requires exponentially many iterations in the worst case to maximize a convex objective of the form $(x_1)^{1+\epsilon}+\vec c^{\top}\vec x$ subject to linear constraints, regardless of the pivot rule used. Our lower bound therefore holds for objectives arbitrarily close to the linear case $\epsilon=0$, where the active-set method coincides with the simplex method and a lower bound for all pivot rules would constitute a major breakthrough. The special case $\epsilon=1$ yields a lower bound in convex quadratic maximization. This improves on the best previously known lower bound [IPCO 2025] requiring polynomial objectives of degree $\omega(\log d)$ in dimension $d$ and firmly resolves the open question of whether a constant degree suffices. Our result is based on a novel extended formulation, recursively constructed using deformed products. Its key feature is that it projects onto a polygonal approximation of a parabola while preserving all of its exponentially many vertices. We define a convex objective with a single non-linear variable that forces the active-set method to follow the parabolic boundary of this projection, without allowing any shortcuts along chords corresponding to edges of its full-dimensional preimage.

papers.title: Improved Lower Bounds on Tree Covers
papers.abstract: A tree cover of an $n$-point metric space is a collection of $k$ trees such that every pairwise distance is approximately preserved in at least one tree. For fixed $k$, the best known distortion upper bound is $\tilde{O}(n^{1/k})$ and the best known lower bound is $\Omega_k(n^{1/2^{k-1}})$. In this paper, we prove a lower bound of $\Omega_k(n^{1/(k-1)^2})$ for all $k\ge 3$, significantly narrowing the gap towards the upper bound. Our approach makes use of a novel algebraic topological notion that we call the \emph{agreement index}: the equivariant topological index of a simplicial complex encoding pairwise agreement among tree labels. This notion helps characterize the power and limit of algebraic and topological methods for analyzing tree covers, and we believe it will also find applications to other problems.

papers.title: Notes on a strongly aperiodic monotile in $E^3$
papers.abstract: We provide a clearer presentation of the Chair44 monotile, a new strongly aperiodic monotile in three-dimensional Euclidean space $E^3$.

papers.title: Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions
papers.abstract: How many fixed points does belief propagation have on a binary pairwise model? Over complex parameters, the admissible equations of a finite loopless multigraph form an algebraic family whose generic degree we determine: it is a graph state sum over edge sets without vertices of degree one, each vertex of positive degree contributing one less than its degree. We give two geometric realizations of this state sum. The first is the total Betti number of a universal edge-incidence ring constructed without parameters. Its full graded Betti table is the state sum, its Tor algebra is natural for noncontracting graph maps, the alternating numerator recovers the graph polynomial of Watanabe and Fukumizu, and an Artin reduction by a regular sequence realizes the one-variable specialization, corrected for tree components. The second lies in the actual family: at the strong-field boundary each state factor is a ramification index, and at sufficiently strong field the state charts exhaust the admissible complex fiber. For fixed nonzero real couplings, every Eulerian message-sign sector contains a real fixed point at every external field, and strong fields attain this lower bound: one admissible real fixed point per element of the binary cycle space and one positive fixed point. For graphs of maximum degree at most three, this minimum equals the number of minimal module generators of the edge-incidence ring. One state decomposition connects the complex degree, graded syzygies, and an attained minimum real count. The degree, selected ring and resolution statements, and the real counts are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: A combinatorial description of when a self-associated set of points fails to be arithmetically Gorenstein
papers.abstract: We give a combinatorial proof that the set of points associated to a self-dual code with no proportional columns is arithmetically Gorenstein if and only if the code is indecomposable. This answers a question asked by Toh\u{a}neanu. We do so by providing a combinatorial way to compute the dimension of the Schur square of a self-dual code through a zero-one symmetrization of a systematic generator matrix. Our approach also allows us to compute the Gorenstein defect. As a consequence, we obtain a combinatorial characterization of arithmetically Gorenstein self-associated sets of points over an algebraically closed field. We also show that, for any finite field, almost all self-dual codes of large length are indecomposable, and hence their associated sets of points are arithmetically Gorenstein.

papers.title: There are no unexpected toric positroid varieties
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a positroid. We prove that the positroid variety $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to some algebraic torus if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ is regular. In that case, $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to the standard diagonal torus. Thus, there are no unexpected toric positroid varieties.

papers.title: On Open Borel Orbits in Conormal Bundles to Schubert Cells
papers.abstract: Let $C(v)$ denote a Schubert cell in the flag variety $\operatorname{GL}_n/B$, and let $X(w)$ be a Schubert variety containing $C(v)$. Mellit has conjectured that, if $X(w)$ is smooth, the existence of an open $B$-orbit in the conormal bundle to $C(v)$ in $X(w)$ is equivalent to $C(w_0w)$ being contained in the smooth locus of $X(w_0v)$. We prove a stronger version of this conjecture, requiring only that $X(w)$ is factorial. We prove our result by constructing a sequence of graphs associated to the pair $v,w$ such that the existence of a cycle in one of these graphs is equivalent to the non-existence of such an open orbit.

papers.title: Tropical spin Hurwitz numbers
papers.abstract: We introduce a tropical framework for the study of spin Hurwitz numbers and their completed cycles analogues. We use degeneration techniques to obtain an interpretation of spin Hurwitz numbers via tropical covers. We employ the tropical methods to obtain new closed formulae for spin Hurwitz numbers in special cases. Moreover, we employ Fock space techniques to tropicalise completed cycles spin Hurwitz numbers. Using this, we prove that spin Hurwitz numbers admit a piecewise polynomial structure akin to their classical counterparts. We also derive wall--crossing formulae.

papers.title: Toric Varieties from Multiple Zeta Values
papers.abstract: The linear relations among fixed weight multiple zeta values (MZVs) are a well-studied subject in number theory. Elements of putative linear bases for this fixed-weight space are, however, not algebraically independent; they satisfy non-linear relations. We study these relations by approximating them through motivic MZVs, formal MZVs and numerical computations. We show that motivic MZVs in fixed weight span a projective toric variety and explore its geometry. We define an outer approximation to the variety of formal MZVs in fixed weight by introducing toric varieties coming from shuffle and stuffle relations and taking their intersection. We conjecture that this intersection in fact agrees with the variety of formal MZVs and hence conjecturally also with the variety of motivic MZVs. This leads to a novel conjecture on a generating set for the extended double shuffle relations, which we checked computationally up to weight $23$.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
papers.abstract: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
papers.abstract: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.

papers.title: When Polynomial Multiplication Counts Geometry: Schubert Polynomials and Monk's Rule
papers.abstract: We give a geometric introduction to Schubert polynomial multiplication through point-line flags in the complex projective plane. Moving a prescribed point onto a prescribed line gives a family with local equation $au=\lambda$, whose limiting curve has two components. The incidence equations and their local multiplicities give a two-term divisor product, using the standard intersection product on classes of algebraic cycles. Permutation labels and Schubert polynomials express the same decomposition as an instance of Monk's rule. For three incidence conditions, each allowing either a point on a prescribed line or a line through a prescribed point, the product has degree six. Under explicit general-position assumptions, direct construction and local equations give six distinct solutions of multiplicity one.

papers.title: Helly theorems for lattice of flats of a matroid
papers.abstract: A basis of a matroid is adapted to a flat if it contains a basis of the flat. We prove that a family of flats in a rank r matroid has a common adapted basis whenever every subfamily of at most r+1 flats does. The ground set and the family may be infinite; only the rank must be finite. This result, in particular, contains Klyachko's vector space Helly theorem for subspaces. As an application, we obtain a splitting criterion for tropical toric vector bundles on projective spaces. As a secondary application, we derive quadratic bounds for the Helly number for distributive generation in the lattice of flats.

papers.title: From amplituhedra to flagtopes
papers.abstract: The amplituhedron was introduced by Arkani-Hamed and Trnka (2014) to geometrically encode scattering amplitudes in high-energy physics. It can be viewed as the generalization of a cyclic polytope into the Grassmannian, and is defined to be the projection of the totally nonnegative part of one Grassmannian with respect to a totally negative element of a second Grassmannian. We construct a Lie-theoretic generalization of amplituhedra called 'flag amplituhedra', by replacing the pair of Grassmannians in the definition with an arbitrary pair of partial flag varieties for a reductive group $G$. We study in detail an example of a flag amplituhedron which is not a Grassmannian amplituhedron; it is a curved hexagon in $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^1$.

papers.title: Generic tensor products are not maximal
papers.abstract: We construct tensor products of uniform matroids which are strictly freer than their generic linear tensor products. In particular, the generic tensor product of two copies of $U_{7,9}$ is not maximal. More generally, for every $a,b\ge2$, this holds for $U_{7,a+7}$ and $U_{7,b+7}$. The construction disproves the uniform tensor-product formulation of Mason's conjecture. Its dual is a relaxation of an explicit circuit-hyperplane of a generic birigidity matroid. By the author's representability theorem, the resulting matroids are non-representable over every field. We also obtain full-rank counterexamples to the Jackson--Tanigawa hyperconnectivity conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$.

papers.title: Average eccentricity in k-connected tournaments
papers.abstract: The average eccentricity $\avec(D)$ of a strong digraph $D$ is the mean eccentricity of all vertices in $D$. A tournament $T$ is an orientation of a complete graph. In this paper, we prove that the average eccentricity satisfies $2 \le \avec(T) < \frac{n}{2k} + \frac{11}{2} + \frac{k}{8n}$ for a $k$-connected tournament $T$ of order $n$. We further examine the case for strong tournaments where $k = 1$, and show that $\avec(T) \le \frac{n+11}{2} + \frac{1}{8n}$ for any strong tournament $T$. Moreover, we show that the lower bound $2$ is sharp and that the upper bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant.

papers.title: On Hamilton cycles in quasiprimitive graphs of order $2pq$
papers.abstract: Let $p>q>5$ be primes. We determine the socles and corresponding actions of quasiprimitive imprimitive groups of degree $2pq$, all of which are almost simple. Using this classification, we prove that a connected graph of order $2pq$ admitting a quasiprimitive automorphism group contains a Hamilton cycle, except possibly for three specified families of actions with socle $\PSL(2,p)$ or $\PSL(2,q^2)$.

papers.title: A generalization of pseudocomplementation in semilattices, lattices and posets with 0
papers.abstract: Pseudocomplemented lattices satisfy a lot of nice properties and were studied by a number of algebraists. However, even when a poset P with 0 is not pseudocomplemented, we can assign to every element a of P the set $a^p$ of all maximal elements being orthogonal to a. This assignment $^p$ is a non-trivial operator provided P satisfies the so-called Ascending Chain Condition (ACC). In particular, we investigate this operator when the poset P in question is a semilattice or a lattice. We characterize this operator and describe its properties that turn out to be similar to the corresponding properties of pseudocomplementation. Moreover, we introduce an equivalence relation $\Theta_p$ on P induced by $^p$ similarly as it was done by V. I. Glivenko for distributive pseudocomplemented lattices. Finally, we investigate for which lattices L with 0 satisfying the ACC this equivalence relation turns out to be a congruence and when the quotient lattice $L/\Theta_p$ is complemented respectively modular.

papers.title: Existence of uniformly most reliable two-terminal graphs with distance constraints
papers.abstract: A two-terminal graph is a simple graph equipped with two distinguished vertices, called terminals. Let $T_{n,m}$ be the class consisting of all non-isomorphic two-terminal graphs on $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. Let $G$ be any two-terminal graph in $T_{n,m}$, and let $d$ be any positive integer. For every $\rho\in [0,1]$, the \emph{$d$-constrained two-terminal reliability of $G$ at $\rho$}, denoted $R_G^d(\rho)$, is the probability that $G$ has some path of length at most $d$ joining its terminals after each of its edges is independently deleted with probability $\rho$. We say $G$ is a \emph{$d$-uniformly most reliable two-terminal graph} ($d$-UMRTTG) if for each $H$ in $T_{n,m}$ and every $\rho \in [0,1]$ it holds that $R_{G}^d(\rho)\geq R_{H}^{d}(\rho)$. Previous works studied the existence of $d$-UMRTTG in $T_{n,m}$ when $d$ is greater than or equal to $n-1$, or equivalently, when the distance constraint is dropped. In this work, a characterization of all $1$-UMRTTGs and $2$-UMRTTGs is given. Several structural properties of 3-UMRTTGs are established. For every $d\geq 3$, we prove the existence of a unique $d$-UMRTTG in $T_{n,\binom{n}{2}-1}$. In contrast, for every $d\geq 4$ and every $n\geq 11$, no $d$-UMRTTG exists in $T_{n,m}$ whenever $20\leq m\leq 3n-9$ or $3n-5\leq m\leq \binom{n}{2}-2$. Additionally, for each $d\geq 5$, it is proved that no $d$-UMRTTG exists in $T_{n,m}$ when $n\geq 11$ and $m=3n-8$.

papers.title: Trace-minimal graphs maximizing the number of spanning trees
papers.abstract:
A classical problem in spectral graph theory is to determine, among all simple graphs with a fixed number of vertices and edges, those that maximize the number of spanning trees. Such graphs are called $t$-optimal. Petingi and Rodr'iguez [Discr. Math. 244 (2002), 351-373] reduced the construction of infinitely many $t$-optimal graphs to the determination of almost-regular graphs with a minimum number of induced $3$-paths, known as almost-regular $
u$-min graphs. They conjectured that the class of $d$-regular $
u$-min graphs is invariant under the addition or deletion of copies of the complete graph $K_{d+1}$, which would provide a method to construct large families of $t$-optimal graphs. This conjecture was recently verified for $d\in \{1,2,3,4,5\}$ by Gong et al. [Discr. Math. 349(4), 2026]. In this work, we establish an asymptotic version of this conjecture. We prove that the class of $d$-regular $
u$-min graphs on at least $n$ vertices is invariant under the addition or deletion of copies of $K_{d+1}$ whenever $d\geq 3$ and $n\geq d^3$. In addition, we introduce a new method to construct $t$-optimal graphs based on the concept of trace-minimal graphs, originally introduced by 'Abrego et al. [Linear Algebra Appl. 412 (2006), 161-221]. As a consequence, we obtain infinitely many graphs that are both trace-minimal and $t$-optimal.

papers.title: A new infinite family of covers of complete graphs that admit a half-transitive action of a Suzuki simple group
papers.abstract: We construct a new infinite family of antipodal $2(q-1)$-covers of complete graphs $K_{q^2+1}$ of diameter $3$, where $q=2^{2e+1}\ge 8$, admitting a half-transitive action of the Suzuki simple group $Sz(q)$. We further show that each constructed cover admits an involutory automorphism interchanging the two $Sz(q)$-orbits on arcs, which yields that its full automorphism group is arc-transitive.

papers.title: Mutation-acyclicity in rank four is decidable but not semialgebraic
papers.abstract: We prove that mutation-acyclicity of quivers on four vertices is decidable. If a four-vertex quiver $Q$ is mutation-acyclic, then some sequence of mutations takes it to an acyclic quiver without any arrow multiplicity exceeding $\operatorname{max}\{\operatorname{ht}(Q),m(Q)\}$, where $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ is the largest arrow multiplicity of $Q$ and $m(Q)$ is the Markov invariant of Fomin and Neville evaluated on the totally proper wiggle class of $Q$. A search within a computable form of this bound decides mutation-acyclicity of four-vertex quivers with $O(h^{24})$ states for input height $h\ge1$. Together with a theorem of Caldero and Keller, it also decides mutation equivalence of two four-vertex quivers up to relabeling whenever one of them is mutation-acyclic. We conjecture that $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ alone suffices as the bound, which would reduce the search to $O(h^{6})$ states, and we verify this for all four-vertex quivers of height at most three. In the other direction, for every $n\ge4$ we construct an affine family of connected $n$-vertex quivers whose nonnegative even members are mutation-acyclic and whose positive odd members are mutation-cyclic. Consequently, unlike in rank three, no fixed finite Boolean combination of polynomial equations and strict polynomial inequalities in the arrow weights (i.e., a semialgebraic criterion) decides mutation-acyclicity of $n$-vertex quivers, even allowing polynomials that are not mutation-invariant. Finally, we correct the criterion for four-vertex quivers of height at most two stated in our earlier paper, and recover its classification counts with short certificates. The calculations in the proof of the height bound are verified by computer for all values of their parameters.

papers.title: On the diameter and distribution of Sidon sets
papers.abstract: A Sidon set is a set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers with the property that if $0\neq a-b=c-d$ and $a,b,c,d\in\mathcal{A}$, then $(a,b)=(c,d)$. Our main result is an improved and explicit bound on the diameter of a Sidon set: if $\mathcal{A}$ is a Sidon set with $k\ge 1$ elements, then \[\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge k^2 \left(\frac{1}{1 + 0.945/\sqrt{k}}-\frac{0.945}{\sqrt k}\right) -1;\] in particular, $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A})\ge k^2-1.89 k^{3/2}$. This implies that if $\mathcal{A}\subseteq[1,N]$ is a Sidon set, then $|\mathcal{A}| \le N^{1/2}+0.945 \, N^{1/4}+0.447$. Our technique also gives an improved bound for the case of large $k$, namely $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge k^2-1.88607 k^{3/2}$ for $k\ge 483$. A $\gamma$-Golomb ruler is a set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers with the property that there are not $\gamma+1$ distinct pairs $(a_i,b_i)\in\mathcal{A}^2$ with $0\neq a_1-b_1=\cdots=a_{\gamma+1}-b_{\gamma+1}$. Our diameter bounds extend in a natural way to the case of Golomb rulers. Our techniques can also be adapted to address a number of questions on the distribution of Golomb rulers: we provide upper bounds on the two quantities $\left|a_\ell-a_1 -\frac{\ell-1}{k-1}(a_k-a_1)\right|$ and $\max_{1\le i<k} (a_{i+1}-a_i)$, where $\mathcal{A}=\{a_1<\dots<a_k\}$ is a $\gamma$-Golomb ruler with $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A})\le (k^2-bk^{3/2})/\gamma$ (where $b\in \mathbb{R}$ is a free parameter).

papers.title: Characterizing $3$-graphs with Degenerate Codegree Tur\'an Density
papers.abstract: Determining the Tur\'an densities $\pi(F)$, uniform Tur\'an densities $\pi_{\therefore}(F)$, and codegree Tur\'an densities $\gamma(F)$ of $3$-graphs $F$ is a notoriously difficult problem in combinatorics. A landmark result by Erd\H{o}s characterized the $3$-graphs whose Tur\'an density is zero. Half a century later, Reiher, R\"{o}dl, and Schacht characterized the $3$-graphs whose uniform Tur\'an density is zero. Recently, Ding, Lamaison, Liu, Wang, and Yang suggested a possible characterization of $3$-graphs whose codegree Tur\'an density is zero, proved one direction of it, and conjectured the other. In this work we confirm this conjecture, completing the characterization of $3$-graphs with codegree Tur\'an density zero. A particular difficulty of this result is that it is known that there are $3$-graphs with arbitrarily small codegree Tur\'an density, contrasting the behavior of the normal and the uniform Tur\'an density. Similar results were independently announced by Chen, Fang, and Yang.

papers.title: Edge complexity of complete bipartite and complete multipartite graphs
papers.abstract: We study edge complexity, the minimum Fourier $\ell^1/\ell^2$ ratio of a graph's adjacency matrix over cyclic vertex labelings. For $K_{m,n}$, with $1\leq m\leq n$, we reduce the problem to minimizing the Fourier $\ell^1$-norm of indicators of $m$-element subsets of $\mathbb Z_{m+n}$. We prove the sharp bound $\operatorname{FR}_{\min}(K_{m,n})\geq\frac{4n^2}{(m+n)\sqrt{2mn}}$, with equality precisely when $m\mid n$, and classify all labelings attaining it. We determine all Fourier ratios and minimizing labelings for $K_{2,n}$, and all minimizing labelings for $K_{3,n}$. Put $N=n+3$. The optimal three-element sets are precisely the cosets of the subgroup of order $3$ in $\mathbb Z_N$ when $3\mid N$, and precisely the arithmetic progressions with invertible common difference otherwise. The triple classification uses polynomial minorants and additive energies. We prove that attainment of the graph-energy bound is invariant under uniform independent set blow-ups. Edge complexity itself can decrease by an arbitrarily large factor under a twofold blow-up, and we give a finite example. For complete multipartite graphs, we give an exact labeling formula and sharp lower bound, and classify all part sizes and labelings attaining that bound. This bound strictly improves the graph-energy bound when the part sizes are unequal. We prove a lower bound for arbitrary simple graphs in terms of their average degree and maximum absolute degree deviation. For Laplacian projectors, we apply the equality criterion for the multiplicity bound to unbalanced complete bipartite graphs, whose top-projector minimum reduces to the same set minimization. Finally, we apply existing Fourier recovery and sampling theorems to approximate a graph from random adjacency samples under a fixed known labeling with bounded Fourier ratio, bounding the number of incorrectly recovered edges.

papers.title: Cops and Robbers on Graphs without Long or Short Holes
papers.abstract: In 2019, Sivaraman conjectured that every $P_k$-free graph has cop number at most $k-3$ for $k\geq 5$. Chudnovsky, Norin, Seymour, and Turcotte proved $P_5$-free graphs have cop number at most $2$. For $k\geq 6$ Sivaraman's conjecture remains widely open. There is little evidence to believe Sivaraman's conjecture is optimal, making the discovery of substantially better bounds interesting, even for subclasses of $P_k$-free graphs. We consider this problem for graphs with no long holes, which generalizes $P_k$-free graphs, that also have some forbidden shorter holes. Specifically, we show that for $t\geq 13$, $(C_4,\dots, C_{t}, C_k,C_{k+1},\dots)$-free graphs have cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-2}{\lfloor \frac{t}{4}\rfloor }\rceil+1$. Taking $C_{k-1}$, which has cop number $2$ whenever $k\geq 5$, demonstrates that this bound is tight up to a small constant factor for infinity many pairs $k$ and $t$. The proof relies on showing that in graphs without short holes, the closed neighbourhood of a short induced path can be guarded by $1$ cop, even when these paths are not geodesics. Additionally, for $t\geq 2$ we show that $(C_{t+2},C_{t+3},C_k, C_{k+1},\dots, )$-free graphs have cop number at most $(t-1)\lceil \frac{(k-2)}{t}\rceil$. This show that $(C_4,C_5,C_k,C_{k+1},\dots)$-free graphs have cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-2}{2}\rceil$, extending work by Clow and Meger on $(P_k,\text{claw}, \text{butterfly}, C_4,C_5)$-free graphs to a substantially more general class.

papers.title: Morse-Maxwell Theory for Directed Acyclic Graph
papers.abstract: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph is obtained from its iterated basin and hill boundaries. The unweighted counts of extrema at these levels need not satisfy Morse inequalities. We assign multiplicities by the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain the vertices with nonzero local homology. The resulting graph preserves both boundary hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its descending and ascending Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We also construct a Morse chain complex and compute the local groups in several examples. Finally, we consider homology on the original Maxwell graph and prove analogous inequalities for path homology using relative local groups.
